When does my January loan actually land?

Fri 20 Nov
·
2 min read

TL;DR

Student Finance England pays your Maintenance Loan at the start of each term. For NTU's standard undergrad courses, Term Two starts Mon 11 Jan 2027, but your own payment date lives in your SFE account.

The overdraft is looking nervous and the group chat has one question: when does the next loan actually hit? Here's the honest answer, with sources.

Start of term, not one national payday

If you're a full-time undergrad funded by Student Finance England (SFE), your Maintenance Loan comes in instalments. GOV.UK's 2026/27 loan terms
(opens in a new tab)
 put it simply: “Maintenance Loans are paid directly to you at the start of each term.” If your course started in the autumn, the second instalment normally lands at the start of your second term, which is generally January.

There's no single January date for everyone, though. Universities tell the Student Loans Company when their students are actually in study, and SLC's guidance for universities
(opens in a new tab)
 says getting those term dates right “will make sure your students get paid at the right time.”

What that means at NTU

NTU's published term dates
(opens in a new tab)
 list Term Two for standard undergraduate courses as Monday 11 January to Friday 19 March 2027. NTU's further-education timetables for Mansfield and Brackenhurst start on 4 January, and NTU itself warns that “Term dates may vary.”

💡
QUICK TIP

A term date isn't a payment promise. Sign in to your Student Finance England account
(opens in a new tab)
 to check when your payments are due, then use that date.

How Til Loan Day uses it

Til Loan Day starts with Mon 11 Jan 2027 as an estimate for NTU undergrads. Put your own date in Your numbers, and your safe daily spend, the day calendar and every “Can I say yes?” preview recalculate around it. 💷

Facts checked on Fri 20 Nov 2026 against the sources linked above. General information, not financial or legal advice.
